chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ubaydi, from Zakariya al-Mumin, from Ali ibn Abi Na'im, from Abu Hamzah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, God, the Blessed and Sublime, says: 'O son of Adam! I have honored you with three things: I covered up for you [your faults]; had your family known about them, they would not have buried you. I granted you ease [in sustenance], then I took a loan from you, yet you did not hasten to do good. I gave you discretion [in making a will] regarding one-third of your wealth at the time of your death, yet you did not hasten to do good.'

key_terms.اسْتَقْرَضْتُكَ: I took a loan from you (metaphor for sustenance)
key_terms.نَظَرَةً: Discretion/choice (specifically regarding the one-third for will)

ai.seo_question: What are the three things God honored the Children of Adam with according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) elucidates three divine favors: the concealment of human faults (satr), sustenance as a loan (qard) to be repaid with good deeds, and the right to bequeath one-third of one's estate. This narration highlights the theological concept of divine generosity despite human negligence, a theme central to Shia discussions on God's mercy (rahmah) and the practical obligations of inheritance and charity.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-150 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Muhammad ibn Isa al-Ubaydi, on the authority of Zakariya (ibn Muhammad) al-Mumin, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Na’eem, on the authority of Abi Hamzih that Abi Ja’far al-Baqir (MGB)

that the Blessed the Sublime God said, “O Children of Adam! I have honored you with three characteristics: I have covered up some of your ugliness. Had your family known about them, they would not have buried you in the ground. I granted you an extension of sustenance. Then I asked you for a loan. You did not rush to do good. I granted you a choice to make a will as to how one third of your property should be spent after your death. But, you did not rush to do good.”
